subject: Neptune Financial — on-prem site: nodepools, storage tiers, and network surface planning
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@neptune-fin.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@neptune-fin.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment inquiry — inventory and high-level needs

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing to host Redwood's inference runtime in our datacenter (NYC) for a scoped pilot. Initial constraints and asks:

- Traffic: ~200 TPS bursty during business hours, steady 20–30 TPS off-hours.
- Models: a mix of medium-sized decoders — peak sequence lengths 1k tokens. We plan to host 2 model families.
- Hardware: we have racks with 4 x A100-style GPUs per chassis (customer labels them "gpu-rack-01"), plus several 192GB RAM CPU-only hosts.
- Storage: local NVMe available on GPU chassis (2 TB), a shared SAN (iSCSI) for larger model store, and an NFS appliance for logs/backups.
- Network: existing L3 fabric in place; egress to internet goes through a perimeter NAT and a pair of stateful firewalls.
- Compliance: SOC 2 in-scope; encryption at rest and audit logs required.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Recommended nodepool breakdown (inference, runtime, control, infra) and affinity strategy for tenant isolation?
2) Where should model weights live (local NVMe vs SAN)? Tradeoffs for perf vs recoverability?
3) Storage class and PVC strategy for large (>100GB) model artifacts and per-request KV caches.
4) Network requirements (CNI, egress rules, BGP/NAT) and whether we need a dedicated egress gateway for policy auditing.

Attaching our simple inventory CSV to speed review. Can we get a short checklist or preflight doc before our technical workshop next week?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Director, Platform Engineering
Neptune Financial

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@neptune-fin.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T12:28:00-04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment inquiry — inventory and high-level needs

Rajiv —

Appreciate the inventory and clear asks. Attached is a concise preflight checklist we've found helpful for pilot sites (redwood-preflight-checklist-v1.pdf). High-level answers before the workshop:

- Nodepools: split into three logical pools: inference-gpu (pinned GPUs, local NVMe caching), runtime-cpu (high-mem for tokenization, batching, scheduler), and infra (kube-proxy, Loki/Prometheus, CSI controllers). We'll propose a separate small control-plane (3 nodes) unless you prefer an air-gapped managed option.

- Model weights: primary copy should live on a resilient SAN for durability and backups; use NVMe as a read-through cache on inference nodes for hot model shards. That gives best perf with recoverability.

- PVC strategy: two storage classes — fast-local-nvme (ReadWriteOnce, local), and durable-block-san (ReadWriteOnce or ReadWriteMany via CSI with an NFS gateway). Recommend PV reclaim=Retain for model artifacts, and TTL-based ephemeral volumes for per-request caches.

- Networking: Calico for policy + BGP peering with leaf switches for pod IP advertising; egress via a dedicated NAT gateway for audit and SNAT controls. We recommend an egress gateway paired with a sidecar policy for additional observability.

Can we schedule a 90-min technical workshop tomorrow afternoon? Karthik and Soojin will lead the infra and storage segments.

Action items for Neptune before the workshop: inventory confirmation, firewall egress lists, and permission to run an iperf test between one GPU chassis and a Redwood test client.

Notes: attaching the checklist.

—Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-preflight-checklist-v1.pdf (stub)

Date: 2026-09-14T14:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment inquiry — inventory and high-level needs

Laura — thanks, that reads well. Quick clarifications:

- We prefer customer-run control plane (security team won't allow managed control plane for pilot). We'll aim for 3 control-plane nodes with etcd replication on dedicated hosts.
- For model durability, SAN is fine but our SAN throughput can be a bottleneck under load — happy to run preflight io tests.
- SOC 2: we need KMS integration (we have HashiCorp Vault with HSM), and audit events forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk).

We can do tomorrow 16:00 EDT for the workshop — Sophie, Karthik and Soojin on the call works. I'll attach our firewall rule export after this email.

—Rajiv

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@neptune-fin.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:41:00-04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment inquiry — inventory and high-level needs

Rajiv / Laura — follow-up with a concrete nodepool and storage proposal ahead of tomorrow's workshop. Key recommendations (summary):

1) Cluster topology
- Control plane: 3x m8.large-equivalent (no GPUs), dedicated etcd on separate NICs.
- Nodepool: inference-gpu (GPU pinned, 4 GPUs/chassis), each node mounts a local NVMe (fast-local-nvme) used as a read-through cache for model shards; also mount durable-block-san for model staging and cold storage.
- Nodepool: runtime-cpu (8–16 vCPU, 192GB RAM hosts) for batching, tokenizer, and CPU-only model variants.
- Nodepool: infra (2–3 nodes) for logging/monitoring/CSI drivers and housekeeping workloads.

2) Storage patterns
- Model artifacts: durable-block-san (CSI) as the canonical source; persist with PV reclaim=Retain and snapshot schedule to SAN backups nightly.
- Hot model cache: fast-local-nvme (StorageClass fast-local-nvme, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer), implement an LRU cache in the redis-like shard loader; preload most-used shards on node startup.
- KV/cache: use ephemeral volumes with TTL (emptyDir for memory-backed caches, or ephemeral PVCs for larger per-request state).

3) Performance & recovery tradeoffs
- Expect local-NVMe read latencies ~100–200us; SAN reads depend heavily on SAN controller (measure IOPS under concurrent reads). Plan a capacity test: 16 concurrent model streams, 1k tokens @ 50ms p95 target.

4) Networking & security
- CNI: Calico BGP for pod routing, enable NetworkPolicies default-deny.
- Egress: dedicated egress gateway with NAT for audit; route all outbound via a pair of HA proxies and record SNAT mapping in logs.
- KMS: integrate with Vault via KMIP/HSM plugin; Redwood runtime will encrypt model caches at rest and rotate keys per policy.
- Audit: forward k8s events and runtime traces to your SIEM (Splunk) over TLS to our ingest endpoint.

Attachments: I created a short workbook (neptune-nodepool-proposal.xlsx) with sizing and recommended instance counts. We'll review the numbers in the workshop.

—Karthik
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: neptune-nodepool-proposal.xlsx (stub)

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@neptune-fin.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T17:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment inquiry — inventory and high-level needs (next steps & MAP)

Rajiv / Sophie — thanks for the workshop earlier today. This thread captures agreed next steps and owners: 

- Neptune: confirm firewall rules and share SAN performance metrics (Rajiv) — due 2026-09-20.
- Redwood: provide a bootstrapping playbook (kubeadm manifests, CSI recipes, calico-bgp guide) and a sample Ansible job to populate local NVMe caches (Laura) — draft by 2026-09-18.
- Redwood infra: run a short load profile (iperf + model load test) against one GPU chassis — coordinate with Neptune ops (Karthik) — test window 2026-09-21.
- Security: KMS integration runbook and audit-event mapping to Splunk (Soojins) — draft by 2026-09-22.

Risks discussed: SAN throughput under multi-node parallel model loads; need for pre-warming model shards during cache misses; and firewall rules that unblock Redis/CSI traffic. We've logged these in the HubSpot deal and the Confluence page (links above).

I'll circulate a consolidated MAP doc later today and open the onboarding Jira ticket for the pilot (SUP-3329). If anything urgent, ping me directly.

—Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
